description: The image displays two side-by-side bar charts comparing Fleiss Kappa scores under different conditions related to ambiguity, likely from a study on defending against social engineering attacks using large language models. The left chart plots Fleiss Kappa on the y-axis (ranging from 0.0 to 0.8 in 0.2 increments) against “Ambiguity Std” values on the x-axis (0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94), with four dark to medium blue bars showing Kappa values of 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24 respectively, indicating a sharp drop at 0.82 followed by a slight recovery. The right chart plots Fleiss Kappa (same y-axis scale) against “Max Ambiguity” levels (1, 2, 3), with three bars showing Kappa values of 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23, revealing a steady decline as ambiguity increases. Both charts use solid-colored bars with exact values labeled atop each bar, and the right chart’s x-axis is labeled “Max Ambiguity” while the left’s is partially obscured but contextually labeled “Ambiguity Std.” The visual trend in both charts suggests that higher ambiguity correlates with lower inter-rater agreement (Fleiss Kappa), with the highest agreement observed at the lowest ambiguity levels.
